Theme

Nature & food · Household, washing & chores

weed noun

an unwanted plant

also weeds, darnel, tares

classical

Verg. G. 1.69: officiant laetīs nē frūgibus herbae (Lewis & Short)
Verg. G. 2.251 (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 18.300 (Lewis & Short)

herba, herbae f.

noun, first declension

a weed (where the sense is clear); weeds: herbae

Latin has no separate word: herba, any green plant, is used of the useless ones that choke a crop (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • lolium, loliī n. — darnel, the weed of cornfields

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 1.154: īnfēlīx lolium et sterilēs dominantur avēnae (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 18.153 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • officiant laetīs nē frūgibus herbae

    so that weeds may not choke the thriving cropsVerg. G. 1.69 (Lewis & Short)

  • īnfēlīx lolium et sterilēs nāscuntur avēnae

    wretched darnel and barren wild oats come upVerg. E. 5.37

See also weed, grass, plant, thistle, bur, nettle.

SourcesLewis & Short: herba · Lewis & Short: lolium

Vergil, Eclogae 5.37.
